title: Striped Hero & Onboarding Flow — First Impression Assets
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a distinctive, high-conversion hero module and a compact onboarding flow visual system for the Quickstart landing page. Deliverables include a striped/stacked hero composition (dark and light themes), three linear step diagrams for starter flows, component-level screenshot templates (desktop/tablet/mobile), motion spec for micro-interactions, and export-ready assets and tokens. Work should prioritize clarity for new developer sign-ups, emphasize fast time-to-value, and produce components that are easy for the frontend team to implement and iterate on.
acceptance_criteria: Figma file with organized pages: hero, steps, screenshots, tokens, motion
Hero art exported in 2 themes (light/dark) and 3 widths (1200px, 900px, 640px)
Step diagrams exportable as SVG and PNG with editable text layers
Responsive screenshot templates covering 1440, 1024, and 375 widths with placeholder copy and annotated specs
Motion spec (timings, easing, Lottie demo) uploaded to Figma prototype and documented in Confluence
Frontend handoff checklist with CSS token mapping and accessibility notes
tasks: Audit existing quickstart assets and collect common patterns
Sketch 6 hero layout concepts and pick top 2 for exploration
Define striped visual language (color bands, micro-ornaments, alignment grid)
Design step-diagram variants: linear cards, vertical ladder, progressive chips
Build responsive screenshot templates and generate sample product screenshots
Document motion spec and create 5 micro-interactions: hero fade, stripe parallax, CTA hover, step reveal, progress microcopy animation
Prepare handoff bundle: tokens.json, asset-exports.zip, implementation notes

decisions: Adopt striped horizontal bands for hero (supports imagery and CTA anchor) to distinguish Quickstart from product pages
Use neutral primary CTA with subtle accent stroke to pass contrast checks and reduce visual noise
Keep step diagrams linear (left-to-right) on desktop and stacked collapsible cards on mobile to preserve scanability
Export vector-first assets and provide PNG fallbacks for old integration points
tradeoffs: Chosen striped approach reduces room for large illustration, may limit brand storytelling but improves scannability and faster A/B testing
Motion will be lightweight (subtle parallax + opacity) to keep performance budgets tight on the marketing site
Providing many responsive breakpoints increases handoff work but prevents engineering rework later

Engineering (Noah Greene): Requested explicit CSS token names and implementation-ready SVGs to avoid pixel drift

Brand (Sofia Alvarez): Approved overall tone but asked to reduce neon accent to align with enterprise audience
